target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures describe the regulatory rule limiting subsidiary bank dividends to current net profits plus retained net profits from the preceding two years. D338 cites OCC definition in 2023; D345 cites same OCC definition in 2024.

D338 provides the specific 2024 dividend capacity for BANA (~$12.0B). D346 provides the specific 2025 dividend capacity for BANA (~$13.0B). Both disclose the forward-looking dividend capacity of the same subsidiary under the same regulatory framework.

peer_results.rationale: Candidate c_2024_8_D207 concerns U.K. revenue figures and c_2024_8_D286 concerns restructuring charges; neither addresses subsidiary dividend capacity or regulatory restrictions on intercompany payments.

comparisons.peer_summary: Group Inc. may be limited in accessing capital at subsidiaries due to regulatory, tax, or other constraints, including laws requiring prior regulatory approval for dividends. For example, GS Bank USA's dividend payments are capped by earnings and undivided profits tests.
comparisons.comparison: While BAC quantifies its specific 2025 dividend capacity, GS discusses the regulatory constraints that limit such capacities generally. GS highlights that regulatory requirements, such as earnings and undivided profits tests for GS Bank USA, cap the ability to declare dividends without prior approval, which is the same regulatory mechanism underlying BAC's disclosed capacity.

sentences.text: In 2025, BANA can declare and pay dividends of approximately $13.0 billion to the Corporation plus an additional amount equal to its retained net profits for 2025 up to the date of any such dividend declaration.

These limitations include provisions of applicable law and regulations and other regulatory restrictions that limit the ability of those subsidiaries to declare and pay dividends without prior regulatory approval.
For example, the amount of dividends that may be paid by GS Bank USA are limited to the lesser of the amounts calculated under a recent earnings test and an undivided profits test.

comparisons.peer_summary: At January 1, 2025, the Parent Company's banking subsidiaries had approximately $15.5 billion in undistributed dividends available without regulatory approval, supplemented by 2025 earnings.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM disclose specific dollar amounts of dividend capacity available to their parent companies in 2025, which consists of a base amount of undistributed dividends supplemented by current year earnings. BANA declares approximately $13.0 billion plus retained net profits, while JPM's subsidiaries have approximately $15.5 billion plus earnings available. Both disclosures frame this capacity as the amount available without requiring prior regulatory approval.

sentences.text: In 2025, BANA can declare and pay dividends of approximately $13.0 billion to the Corporation plus an additional amount equal to its retained net profits for 2025 up to the date of any such dividend declaration.

At January 1, 2025, the Parent Company's banking subsidiaries could pay, in the aggregate, approximately $15.5 billion in dividends to their respective bank holding companies without the prior approval of their relevant banking regulators.
The capacity to pay dividends in 2025 will be supplemented by the banking subsidiaries' earnings during the year.
